definitions.explanation: Hagoromo Foods' trademark for canned tuna in oil, so widely used that many people say it for any canned tuna. The name, "sea chicken", refers to the pale, mild meat.

examples.japanese: シーチキン⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{缶|かん}→缶：01076_kan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|あ}ける→開ける：00563_akeru⟧。
examples.english: To open a can of tuna.

examples.japanese: シーチキン⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦マヨネーズ→マヨネーズ：11129_mayoneezu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦おにぎり→おにぎり：04956_onigiri⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: I made rice balls with canned tuna and mayonnaise.

examples.japanese: ⟦{冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}→冷蔵庫：01046_reizouko⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{何|なに}も→何も：03874_nanimo⟧⟦なかった→ない：01118_nai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、シーチキン⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{玉|たま}ねぎ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{簡単|かんたん}→簡単：00713_kantan⟧な⟦サラダ→サラダ：01364_sarada⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: There was nothing in the fridge, so I made a simple salad with canned tuna and onion.

notes:
A registered trademark of Hagoromo Foods; competing products are labeled ⟦ツナ{缶|かん}→ツナ缶：26947_tsunakan⟧, but in conversation シーチキン often stands for canned tuna in general, much as English speakers say Kleenex.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- シーチキンマヨ / ツナマヨ: tuna with mayonnaise, a standard rice-ball filling
- シーチキン⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{缶|かん}→缶：01076_kan⟧: a can of tuna

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦ツナ→ツナ：09957_tsuna⟧: tuna (canned or prepared); the generic word, used on packaging and menus
- ⟦ツナ{缶|かん}→ツナ缶：26947_tsunakan⟧: canned tuna (generic)
